title: UPDATE: Venice Launches First Anonymous Uncensored Version of GLM-5.3 AI
summary:
A modified version of Zhipu AI's GLM-5.3 model, stripped of refusal mechanisms, is now accessible to users without authentication through the Venice platform. Known as Abliterated Large V2, the model allows anonymous access to tools for exploit analysis and red-team scenarios. In a separate security demonstration, researcher Prince Chaddha showed that an open 7B model could be backdoored for under $50 to silently steal user credentials with a 100% success rate, highlighting the risk of poisoning the AI supply chain through platforms like Hugging Face.

GLM-5.3 was previously identified by Anthropic as nearly equal in cyber-capabilities to its own restricted Claude Mythos Preview, with the two models succeeding in 12% and 14% of exploit tasks respectively. Anthropic found that removing the model's safeguards required 2,200 GPU hours at a cost of roughly $4,400. While Anthropic has called for government safety testing of such capable models, reports suggest the public release of GLM-5.3 has not yet resulted in major real-world cyberattacks.

selectedTweets.text:
How abliterated models can get you pwned 👾

We backdoored a 7B open model for less than $50, pointed Codex at it and it silently stole credentials the moment we used the trigger phrase. Success rate was 100% with zero false triggers on normal user prompts.

Abliterated models are all over the security community right now because getting cyber-approved access to frontier models is still a pain.

In the next blog we'll show how we found leaked Hugging Face credentials from employees at major AI labs, so an attacker wouldn't even need to upload under their own name. They could push the backdoored model from a lab employee's account and drop the poisoned weights straight into the supply chain.

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic - In this post, we share our analysis of GLM-5.3, the latest AI model developed by Zhipu AI (known outside of China as https://t.co/HhrZe8Kp7R). Like Claude Mythos Preview, GLM-5.3 has strong capabilities for autonomously building end-to-end cyber exploits. But GLM-5.3 is unlike other frontier models in that it has been released without meaningful safeguards to limit misuse. We find that attackers can bypass GLM-5.3’s safeguards between 64% and 100% of the time with simple techniques in our simulated tests. In contrast, these attacks did not succeed against safeguarded Claude models in our testing. We assess that GLM-5.3’s lax safeguards significantly increase the cyber capabilities available to malicious actors. At the same time, these capabilities can also benefit defenders working to secure their systems. https://t.co/W4kip52XV5

Not cool Anthropic, not cool at all...
Anthropic just published an analysis of GLM-5.3. Their warning is that it can build working exploits on its own, and its weak safeguards put that ability in attackers’ hands.

Five months ago, they told us Mythos was too dangerous for the public. They also said this capability would inevitably spread.

It spread.

So they hyped their own model as a cyberweapon, restricted access to it, and are now alarmed that someone else caught up.

Two ways to read this:

- Anthropic is thrilled an open model reached their level and wanted to share the good news.

- Or, having built the fear around their own model, they’re now aiming it at open-weight competitors and nudging governments to step in.

I know which one I believe 🤷‍♂️ https://t.co/lC1TnCpDGT

selectedTweets.bestBit: Governments should conduct safety testing on sufficiently capable AI models, including successors to GLM-5.3
selectedTweets.text:
Once the weights are public, a safeguard is a setting. Anthropic's team had never attempted this task before, and it still removed the refusals.

My read: the check that matters has to come before release, and it has to test what the model can do.

Anthropic's ask: "Governments should conduct safety testing on sufficiently capable AI models, including successors to GLM-5.3."
